main_text.p: נִפְרַד Dividi, Disjungi, Separari, Separare se: Præter. נִפְרַד Separaverat se, Jud.4.11. & Kametz est propter pausam: נִפְרַד Divisæ sunt, Gen.10.5. Partic. נִפְרָד Disparans vel separans se, Prov.18.1. id est, Qui animo ab omnibus alieno, & se ex omnium consortio subducit, ut in suo proposito & animi sententia persistat. Pih. Futur. יִפְרוּ Separant, Separationem faciunt, Hos.4.14. Pyh. Partic. מְפֻרָּד Disi-patus, divisus, Eph.3.8. [?] Hiph. הִפְרִיד Separavit, Separationem fecit, Dissipavit, Disjunxit, Diremit: Præter. הִפְרִיד Separabat, Genes.30.40. Partic. מַפְרִיד אֱלוּף [?] Disjungit ducem, Prov.13.9. Infinit. בְּהַפְרִידוֹ Cùm disparet ille, Deut.32.8. Fut. יַפְרִיד Separationem faciet, Ruth.1.17. Hithp. Præter. וְהִתְפָּרְדוּ Et disiparant se offa mea, Psal.22. v.15. Futur. יִתְפָּרְדוּ Disipantur, Psal.92.10.
פֶּרֶד m. Mulus, 2.Sam.18. v.9. Aff. פִּרְדּוֹ Mulum suum, 2.Sam.13.29. Plural. פְּרָדִים Muli, 2.Reg.5.17. Fœmin. פְּרֵדָה Mula, 1.Reg.1.33.

פַּרְדֵּס m. παράδεισος [?], Paradisus, Pomarium, voluptatis & amœnitatis causâ confitum, Cant.4. v.13. At Neh.2.8. Sylvam, Saltum, R.Salom. exponit, quo nomine totam regionem comprehendi volunt Interpretes, à Libano ad Antilibanum, arboribus præstantissimis amœnissimam, in cujus extremitate fuit oppidum nomine Paradisi, cujus meminit Ptolomæus, & Plin.lib.5.cap.23. Plural. פַּרְדֵּסִים Pomaria, Eccles.2.5. ubi notat Aben Esra, jam esse Hortum, qui varias habet species arborum; פַּרְדֵּס vero, qui unicam tantùm; ut, Hortus malorum punicorum, Cantic.4. in quo tantùm fuerunt mala punica. Aliis alter placet.
פָּרָה Fructuosus fuit, Fructum edidit, Fœtavit, Fœtificavit: Præter. פָּרוּ Fœtificaverunt, Exod.1. v.7.

page.notes: Uncertain readings are marked [?]: the Greek headword παράδεισος, the Hebrew of the Pyh. Partic., the Hebrew of the Partic. with "ducem" (Prov.13.9), the headword before "Vide initio Radicis", "Eph.3.8" (the printed letters are unclear), and the Hebrew sign before "v.13." in Cant.4 (printed as a doubtful letter). "Cant.4. v.13." was read as v.13 with doubt. "Disi-patus" is printed with a line break in the word. Entry headword "פֶּרֶד" is partly cut off in the scan. The "v.7." after "Exod.1." stands on its own line at the right and is kept as the continuation of the last entry.
